55.t:
His name: al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿImād (1) ibn Akbar ibn Rabīʿah ibn Muqniʿ ibn Ḥaḍramawt.
He was one of the allies of the Banū Umayyah and one of the chiefs of the Emigrants.
His brother Maymūn ibn al-Ḥaḍramī is the one to whom the Well of Maymūn, in the upper part of Mecca, is attributed; he dug it before the Prophetic mission.
Their other two brothers were ʿAmr and ʿĀmir. ⟦1:262⟧
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed him governor of Bahrain, and then he governed it for Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.
It is said that ʿUmar sent him to take up the governorship of Basra, but he died before reaching it, and after him Abū Hurayrah governed Bahrain for ʿUmar.
He has a hadith: (The Emigrant stays in Mecca after completing his rites: three days (1)).
Narrating from him: السائب بن يزيد.
Also narrating from him: حيان الأعرج، وزياد بن حدير.
روى منصور بن زاذان، عن محمد بن سيرين، عن ابن العلاء:
That al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Ḥaḍramī wrote to the Prophet ﷺ and began with himself (2).
Ibn Isḥāq said: Their father, al-Ḥaḍramī, was an ally of Ḥarb ibn Umayyah, and he was from the land of Ḥaḍramawt.
His name: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbād ibn al-Ṣadaf. ⟦1:263⟧
ابن لهيعة (1) : عن أبي الأسود، عن عروة، قال:
Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq sent him, meaning al-ʿAlāʾ, with an army toward Bahrain, whose people had apostatized. He marched against them, with the sea between him and them, meaning al-Raqrāq, until they walked through it on their feet. They crossed in this way a place where ships used to sail, and ships sail there today as well. He fought them, Allah gave him victory over them, and they paid the zakat.
He died in the year: twenty-one.
It is narrated from Abū Hurayrah:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me with al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Ḥaḍramī and commended me to his care, and I used to call the call to prayer for him (2).
Al-Miswar ibn Makhramah said: The Prophet ﷺ sent al-ʿAlāʾ to Bahrain, then dismissed him in favour of Abān ibn Saʿīd.
Muḥammad ibn Saʿd said: Abū Bakr sent al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Ḥaḍramī, and he set out from Medina with sixteen riders. He wrote for him a letter ordering that every Muslim he passed should march out with him against their enemy.
Al-ʿAlāʾ marched with those who followed him until he reached the fortress of Juwāthā (3). He fought them, and none of them escaped.
Then he came to al-Qaṭīf, where a force had gathered; he fought them and they were routed, and the non-Arabs ⟦1:264⟧ joined al-Zārah. Al-ʿAlāʾ came to them and encamped at al-Khaṭṭ on the seashore; he fought them and besieged them until al-Ṣiddīq died.
Then the people of al-Zārah asked for peace and he made peace with them. Then he fought the people of Dārīn, killed the fighters and took the families.
He sent ʿArfajah to the coast of Persia; he sank the ships, conquered an island in the land of Persia, and built a mosque there (1).
مجالد: عن الشعبي:
That ʿUmar wrote to al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Ḥaḍramī, who was in Bahrain: March to ʿUtbah ibn Ghazwān, for I have appointed you over his post, thinking that you are more self-sufficient than he; so recognize his due.
Al-ʿAlāʾ set out with a company, among them Abū Hurayrah and Abū Bakrah. When they were at Niyās (2), al-ʿAlāʾ died.
Abū Hurayrah used to say: I saw three things in al-ʿAlāʾ because of which I shall never cease to love him:
He crossed the sea on his horse on the day of Dārīn (3); and when he came intending Bahrain, he prayed to Allah at al-Dahnāʾ, and water gushed forth for them and they drank their fill. A man among them forgot some of his belongings and went back, and he found them, but did not find the water. ⟦1:265⟧
And he died while we were without water, so Allah brought forth a cloud for us and it rained on us; we washed him, dug his grave with our swords, buried him, and did not dig a niche for him.

56.h: 52 - Saʿd ibn Khaythamah ibn al-Ḥārith al-Anṣārī al-Awsī *
56.t:
Ibn Mālik ibn Kaʿb ibn al-Naḥḥāṭ ibn Kaʿb ibn Ḥārithah ibn Ghanm ibn al-Salm, Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī, al-Awsī, Badrī (البدري), the chieftain, maternal brother of Abū Ḍayyāḥ (1) al-Nuʿmān ibn Thābit.
His line died out in the year 200.
Ibn al-Kalbī disagreed about al-Naḥḥāṭ and made it al-Ḥannāṭ ibn Kaʿb.
The Prophet ﷺ established brotherhood between him and Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Asad.
They said: He was one of the twelve chieftains.
When the Prophet (2) ﷺ summoned the Muslims on the day of Badr and they hurried, Khaythamah said to his son Saʿd:
Give me preference in going out, and stay with your women.
He refused and said: Were it anything other than Paradise, I would give you preference in it.
So they cast lots, and Saʿd's arrow came out; he went out and was martyred at Badr, and his father Khaythamah was martyred on the day of Uḥud. ⟦1:266⟧

57.h: 53 - al-Barāʾ ibn Maʿrūr ibn Ṣakhr ibn Khansāʾ ibn Sinān al-Khazrajī *
57.t:
The chief, the chieftain, Abū Bishr al-Anṣārī, al-Khazrajī.
He was one of the chieftains on the night of al-ʿAqabah, and he was the son of the paternal aunt of Saʿd ibn Muʿādh.
He was the chieftain of his people, the Banū Salimah.
He was the first to pledge allegiance on the night of the first ʿAqabah, and he was virtuous, God-fearing, and a jurist (الفقيه) at heart.
He died in Ṣafar, a month before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived in Medina.
محمد بن إسحاق: حدثني معبد بن كعب، عن أخيه عبد الله، عن أبيه، قال:
We set out from Medina intending the Prophet ﷺ in Mecca, and with us went the pilgrims of our people who were polytheists, until we reached Dhū al-Ḥulayfah.
Al-Barāʾ ibn Maʿrūr, who was our chief and a man of our customs (1), said to us: By Allah, you know that I have decided not to turn this edifice (2) behind my back, and to pray toward it.
We said: By Allah, we will not do so; it has not reached us that our Prophet prays other than toward Syria, and we would not oppose his qibla.
And indeed I saw him, whenever the prayer came due, pray toward the Kaʿbah.
He said: We reproached him, but he insisted on persisting in it, until we reached Mecca.
Then he said to me: O son of my brother! I have done something ⟦1:267⟧ on my journey and I do not know what it is, so come with me to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and let us ask him about what I did.
We did not know the Messenger of Allah, so we went out asking about him. At al-Abṭaḥ we met a man and asked him about him, and he said: Do you know him?
We said: No.
He said: Do you know al-ʿAbbās?
We said: Yes. Al-ʿAbbās used to visit us for trade, so we knew him.
He said: He is the man sitting with him now in the mosque.
We went to them both, greeted them and sat down, and we asked al-ʿAbbās.
The Messenger of Allah (1) ﷺ said: (Who are these two, uncle?).
He said: This is al-Barāʾ ibn Maʿrūr, the chief of his people, and this is Kaʿb ibn Mālik.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (The poet?).
Al-Barāʾ said: O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I have done such and such.
He said: (You were upon a qibla; had you been patient with it).
So he returned to his qibla.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set an appointment with us for the middle night of al-ʿAqabah ..., and he narrated the story in full (2).
وروى: يحيى بن عبد الله بن أبي قتادة، عن أمه، عن أبيه:
That al-Barāʾ ibn Maʿrūr bequeathed a third of his property to the Prophet ﷺ; he had bequeathed a third in the cause of Allah and a third to his children.
It was reported to the Prophet ﷺ, and he returned it to the heirs.
The Prophet ﷺ arrived after he had died, asked about his grave, and came to it, lined up the people at it and said the takbīr.
And he said: (O Allah, forgive him, have mercy on him, and admit him to Paradise, and I have done so (3)).
On the night of al-ʿAqabah, al-Barāʾ was the most eminent (4) of the seventy and the first of them to pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ⟦1:268⟧ ﷺ, and his son was:

58.h: 54 - Bishr ibn al-Barāʾ ibn Maʿrūr al-Khazrajī *
58.t:
One of the nobles of his people.
It is narrated in the hadith of Abū Hurayrah and Jābir:
That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Who is your chief, O Banū Salimah?).
They said: Al-Jadd ibn Qays, though he has some miserliness.
He said: (And what disease is worse than miserliness? Rather, your chief is the fair, curly-haired one: Bishr ibn al-Barāʾ (1)).
I say: He is the one who ate with the Prophet ﷺ from the poisoned sheep on the day of Khaybar and was afflicted (2), and he was one of the great Badrīs (البدريين). ⟦1:269⟧

59.h: 55 - Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah ibn Dulaym ibn Ḥārithah al-Anṣārī *
59.t:
Ibn Abī Khuzaymah (1) ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Ṭarīf ibn al-Khazraj ibn Sāʿidah ibn Kaʿb ibn al-Khazraj.
The great chief, the noble, Abū Qays al-Anṣārī, al-Khazrajī, al-Sāʿidī, al-Madanī, the chieftain, chief of the Khazraj.
He has few hadiths, twenty counting repetitions.
He died before the time of narration.
Narrating from him: سعيد بن المسيب، والحسن البصري، mursal (مرسل).
Abū Dāwūd and al-Nasāʾī have two hadiths from him (2).
Abū al-Aswad said, from ʿUrwah: that he fought at Badr.
A group said: He did not fight at it. ⟦1:270⟧
Ibn Saʿd said: He was preparing to go out to Badr and used to go to the houses of the Anṣār urging them to go out, but he was bitten by a snake and stayed behind.
The Prophet ﷺ said: (Even if Saʿd did not fight at Badr, he was eager for it (1)).
He said: He was a man of al-ʿAqabah, a chieftain, a chief, and generous.
When the Prophet ﷺ came to Medina, he used to send him every day a bowl of thard with meat, or thard with milk, or other food, and Saʿd's bowl would go round with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ among the houses of his wives.
Al-Bukhārī said in (his History): that he fought at Badr.
Ibn Mandah followed him.
Among those who narrated from him were his sons: Qays, Saʿīd and Isḥāq, and Ibn ʿAbbās.
He settled in Damascus according to what Ibn ʿAsākir transmitted (2).
He said: And he died in Ḥawrān.
It is said: His grave is at al-Munayḥah (3).
روى ابن شهاب، عن عبيد الله، عن ابن عباس، عن سعد بن عبادة:
That his mother died owing a vow, so she asked the Prophet ﷺ, and he commanded me to fulfil it on her behalf (4). ⟦1:271⟧
Most made it part of (Musnad Ibn ʿAbbās).
Aḥmad in (his Musnad): حدثنا يونس، حدثنا حماد، حدثنا عبد الرحمن بن أبي شميلة، عن رجل رده إلى سعيد الصراف، عن إسحاق بن سعد بن عبادة، عن أبيه:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (This tribe of the Anṣār is a shield; love of them is faith and hatred of them is hypocrisy (1)).
Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah and the group said: He was one of the chieftains on the night of al-ʿAqabah.
وعن معروف بن خربوذ (2) ، عن أبي الطفيل، قال:
Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah and al-Mundhir ibn ʿAmr came to bring provisions for the people of al-ʿAqabah, after the people had left; the people of Mecca became aware of them (3), and Saʿd was seized while al-Mundhir escaped.
Saʿd said: They beat me until they left me as though I were a red ⟦1:272⟧ idol-stone, which is reddened by the blood of sacrifices upon it.
He said: Then a man withdrew (1) with me, as though he pitied me, and said:
Woe to you! Do you have no one in Mecca whose protection you can seek?
I said: No, except that al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil used to come to us in Medina and we would honour him.
A man among the people said: He has mentioned my cousin; by Allah, none of you shall reach him.
So they held back from me, and it was ʿAdī ibn Qays al-Sahmī (2).
حجاج بن أرطاة: عن الحكم، عن مقسم، عن ابن عباس، قال:
The banner of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was with ʿAlī, and the banner of the Anṣār was with Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah (3).
Narrated by: أبو غسان النهدي، عن إبراهيم بن الزبرقان، عنه.
معمر: عن عثمان الجزري، عن مقسم - لا أعلمه إلا عن ابن عباس -:
The standard of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to be with ʿAlī, and the standard of the Anṣār with Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah (4).
حماد بن سلمة: عن ثابت، عن أنس، قال:
When the news of Abū Sufyān's return (5) reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: (Advise me).
Abū Bakr stood up.
He said: (Sit down).
Then Saʿd ibn ⟦1:273⟧ ʿUbādah stood up and said: If you ordered us, O Messenger of Allah, to plunge them into the sea, we would plunge them in; and if you ordered us to strike their livers as far as Birk al-Ghimād, we would do it (1).
أبو حذيفة: حدثنا سفيان، عن الكلبي، عن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of Badr: (Whoever brings a prisoner shall have his spoils).
Abū al-Yasar brought two prisoners.
Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah said: O Messenger of Allah! We were guarding you out of fear for you.
Then was revealed: {“They ask you about the spoils of war (2) ”} (Qurʾān 8:1).
Narrated also by: عبد الرزاق، عن سفيان.
علي بن بحر: حدثنا عبد المهيمن بن عباس بن سهل، حدثنا أبي، عن جدي:
That the Prophet ﷺ, when he proposed to a woman and gave her a dowry, would stipulate for her: the bowl of Saʿd goes round with me whenever it goes round to you.
So Saʿd used to send a bowl to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ every night (3).
محمد بن إسحاق بن يسار: عن أبيه — mursal (مرسل), similar to it. ⟦1:274⟧
الأوزاعي: عن يحيى بن أبي كثير:
The Prophet ﷺ had from Saʿd every day a bowl that went round with him wherever he went.
Saʿd used to say: O Allah, provide me with wealth, for noble deeds are set right only by wealth (1).
أحمد: حدثنا يزيد، حدثنا عباد بن منصور، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، قال:
When it was revealed: {“Those who accuse chaste women”} [al-Nūr: 14], Saʿd, the chief of the Anṣār, said:
Was it revealed thus, O Messenger of Allah?
The Prophet ﷺ said: (O company of the Anṣār! Do you not hear what your chief says?).
They said: Do not blame him, for he is a jealous man. By Allah, he never married a woman except a virgin, and never divorced a woman after which anyone dared marry her.
Saʿd said: O Messenger of Allah! By Allah, I know that it is true and that it is from Allah, but I am astonished: if I found a vile woman with a man between her thighs, I would not be permitted to disturb him or move him until I bring four witnesses; and I would not bring them before he has fulfilled his need ... the hadith (2).
And in the hadith of the slander: ʿĀʾishah said:
Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah stood up, he being the chief of the Khazraj, and before that a righteous man, but partisan zeal carried him away (3), and he said:
Never, by Allah! You will not kill him, and you are not able to do that (4). ⟦1:275⟧
Meaning: he was replying to Saʿd ibn Muʿādh, the chief of the Aws.
This is problematic, for Ibn Muʿādh had already died (1).
جرير بن حازم: عن ابن سيرين:
Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah used to return every night to his family with eighty of the People of the Bench, to give them supper.
ʿUrwah said: Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah used to say:
O Allah, grant me praise and glory; O Allah, a little does not set me right, and I do not set right with it (2).
I say: He was a noble king, obeyed, and the Anṣār gathered around him (3) on the day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died to pledge allegiance to him, while he was feverish, until Abū Bakr and the group came and turned them from their view; and that was not pleasing to Saʿd.
Al-Wāqidī: حدثنا محمد بن صالح (4) ، عن الزبير بن المنذر بن أبي أسيد الساعدي:
That al-Ṣiddīq sent to Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah: Come and pledge allegiance, for the people have pledged.
He said: No, by Allah, I will not pledge allegiance to you until I fight you with those who are with me.
Bashīr ibn Saʿd said: O Caliph of the Messenger of Allah! He has refused and persisted; he will not pledge allegiance to you until he is killed, and he will not be killed until his son and his clan are killed with him. So do not stir him as long as the matter remains in your favour; he is only one man on his own, and he does not leave anything. ⟦1:276⟧
So Abū Bakr left him, and when ʿUmar became ruler he met him and said: Well, Saʿd!
He said: Well, ʿUmar!
ʿUmar said: Are you the one who is who you are?
He said: Yes, and this office has come to you; your predecessor, by Allah, was dearer to us than you, and I have come to dislike being your neighbour.
He said: Whoever dislikes that should move away from it.
He stayed only a short while before moving to Syria, and he died in Ḥawrān (1).
Its chain of transmission (الإسناد) is as you see (2).
ابن عون: عن ابن سيرين: That Saʿd urinated standing and died, and a monk was heard saying:
We have killed the chief of the Khaz ... raj, Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah
We shot him with two arrows* ... and did not miss his heart (3)
Saʿd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: Buṣrā was first conquered, and Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah died in it.
Abū ʿUbayd said: He died in the year 14 in Ḥawrān (4).
وروى: ابن أبي عروبة، عن ابن سيرين:
That Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah urinated standing and died, and said: I feel a creeping sensation. ⟦1:277⟧
الأصمعي: حدثنا سلمة بن بلال (1) ، عن أبي رجاء، قال:
Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah was killed in Syria; the jinn shot him in Ḥawrān.
الواقدي: حدثنا يحيى بن عبد العزيز من ولد سعد، عن أبيه، قال:
Saʿd died in Ḥawrān two and a half years into the caliphate (الخلافة) of ʿUmar, and his death was not known in Medina until boys heard someone speaking from a well, saying:
We have killed the chief of the Khaz ... raj, Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah
We shot him with two arrows ... and did not miss his heart
The boys were terrified, and that day was noted, and they found it to be the day on which he died (2).
He had only sat down to urinate in a hole in the ground and died on the spot, and they found his skin had turned green.
Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr, Ibn ʿĀʾishah and others said: He died in Ḥawrān in the year 16.
وروى: المدائني، عن يحيى بن عبد العزيز، عن أبيه، قال:
He died during the caliphate (الخلافة) of Abū Bakr.
Ibn Saʿd said: Saʿd used to write in the Jāhiliyyah (الجاهلية), and was good at swimming and archery, ⟦1:278⟧ and he excelled at those, so he was called al-Kāmil.
Saʿd and several of his forefathers before him used to have a call made from their fortress: Whoever loves fat and meat, let him come to the fortress of Dulaym ibn Ḥārithah (1).
